dialogue.intro:
There is no quest board here, and nobody has assigned you a destiny. There is only this journal.

Some people build somewhere worth returning to. Others keep the horizon for company. Which sounds like your first chapter?
dialogue.complete: The first page is yours. Choose a direction using Story Choices. You can still explore every part of this world; the choice only shapes this little story.

choices.label: Build a place worth returning to
choices.text: You fold a corner of the page. A camp does not need a castle. A table, a light, and a reason to come back will do.

choices.label: Keep the horizon for company
choices.text: You leave the page uncreased. There will be time to settle later. For now, a forest path is enough.

dialogue.intro: A small camp runs on ordinary things. A few logs. A little stone. Accept this contract when you are ready to contribute.
dialogue.progress: The supply box is open. Send what you have; you can finish the delivery later.
dialogue.complete: Enough for another day. Your provisions and satchel are ready. After the cooldown, begin another cycle without erasing your advancement.

dialogue.intro: Before heading out, get moving. This contract starts counting jumps when you accept it.
dialogue.progress: Five jumps. No marked route, no destination. Just a little momentum.
dialogue.complete: Ready for the road. Claim the torches and carry on.

dialogue.intro: Your choice opens the campkeeper chapter. Accept, then make or find a crafting table.
dialogue.complete: A workbench is a modest beginning. It is still a beginning.

dialogue.intro: Your choice opens the wanderer chapter. Accept and find any forest.
dialogue.complete: Leaves overhead. Room to keep walking. The world has plenty of chapters left.

dialogue.intro: The journal starts with something ordinary: a loose piece of stone. Obtain stone using the original Minecraft objective.
dialogue.complete:
Cold in the hand, heavy enough to trust. Stone will not make this world safe, but it gives you somewhere to begin.

The original advancement is still yours. Claim the small field ration when you are ready.

dialogue.intro: A furnace turns patience into possibility. Smelt your first iron ingot; this is the unchanged vanilla trigger.
dialogue.complete: The first ingot catches the firelight. Tools, a bucket, a new direction: the metal promises none of them, but permits all of them.

dialogue.intro: There are stories beyond the circle of light. Follow the original Adventure objectives and let the journal keep the margins.
dialogue.complete: Your first encounter belongs to the same world as every quiet evening. Adventure needs no appointed hero.

dialogue.intro: Small habits keep a camp going. Two sticks are enough to start today’s page.
dialogue.progress: Use Submit Items. Its receipt shows exactly what left your inventory.
dialogue.complete: Today’s page is complete. Claim your ration; tomorrow’s can wait.

dialogue.intro: A camp is easier to keep when everyone lends a hand. This contract keeps one shared tally and one shared reward chest.
dialogue.progress: Use Submit Items. Its receipt shows exactly what left your inventory.
dialogue.complete: The camp has its stone. One participant can collect the group’s provisions. Decide how to share them in the world.

dialogue.intro: This is an ordinary sagittary advancement. Its original objective, requirements, parent and rewards remain owned by the mod. Codex adds this optional journal page. Open Edit Mode to customize the story or attach rewards without converting the tree.
dialogue.progress: Continue with the native objective shown in the advancement. Your mod gameplay remains the source of progress.
dialogue.complete: This page follows your native achievement. The story belongs alongside the mod, while the objective still belongs to it.

dialogue.intro: Any kind of log will help. One piece should carry a name: Camp Timber. You can name an oak log in an anvil, or copy the property from an example while authoring.
dialogue.progress: The delivery receipt names the actual items consumed. A named oak log can satisfy only one outstanding requirement at a time.
dialogue.complete: A small mark turns a supply into a memory.

dialogue.intro: Accept together, contribute to one tally, then collect your own share. The next cycle waits until the remaining participants have claimed.
dialogue.complete: Everyone who stayed with this cycle has a share waiting.

dialogue.intro: A blank page waits for news. Each reply appears when its conditions are met; hover a locked option to read its requirements.
dialogue.complete: The journal can hold news from any kind of play.

choices.label: Tell the camp what you built
choices.text: You describe ordinary materials becoming a place that matters. The reply is short: leave a light for whoever returns next.

choices.label: Write about the unfamiliar horizon
choices.text: Your page carries no coordinates. It carries a reason to keep exploring, and a reminder that you may always return.

dialogue.intro: A compass can help you return without telling you where to go. This page marks a tool, not a prescribed journey.
dialogue.complete: You have a heading of your own. Change the celebration title or sound in the Effects tab to make this milestone yours.
